body:
Can you present an example where the `<script>` is being inserted before `<!DOCTYPE>`. I can't think of a way that could be happening.

We have a lot of tests around this behavior and it should not happen. Cypress waits to figure out the most appropriate place to insert it depending on whether or not it finds an `<html>` tag, a `<head>` tag or a `<body>` tag.

The documents in question contain only a `<!DOCTYPE>` declaration. (That’s because they’re programmatically populated.) Perhaps that’s a case that the existing algorithm doesn’t account for?

The fact that the script gets injected at an unexpected place is just one aspect of the problem, though. Ideally we’d be able to just disable the script injection altogether when necessary.

@brian-mann I encountered this because [our app](https://master-branch-opensphere-ngageoint.surge.sh/) omits `html`, `head`, and `body` in its `index.html` for simplicity. These tags aren't required by spec, but when absent from the page Cypress will insert the `document.domain` script before `<!DOCTYPE>`.

I have created a repo to demonstrate this behavior here: https://github.com/jennifer-shehane/empty-doctype-html ### When no `` #### Application html ```html ``` #### HTML in Cypress (WRONG) ```html ``` ### When `` #### Application html ```html ``` #### HTML in Cypress (CORRECT) ```html ``` ### Failing test in repo

issue.title: Update script injection to handle case where only DOCTYPE declaration in document
